{{Quote|Inform the commander that Lord Vader's shuttle has arrived.|Lieutenant Endicott|<ref name="ROTJ" />}}
'''Endicott''', a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], served aboard the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] as a [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] [[Technician/Legends|technician]] by [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], a position he received after graduating third in his class from the prestigious [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]]. Endicott oversaw the unexpected arrival of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[ST 321/Legends|personal shuttle]] aboard the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] shortly before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. He served in the Death Star's [[Death Star command center|control room]] alongside battlestation [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod/Legends|Tiaan Jerjerrod]] during the battle, witnessing the initial use of the Death Star's [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser|superlaser]] upon the attacking [[Starship/Legends|starships]] of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Alliance Fleet]], and later relayed Jerjerrod's final command to use the Death Star to destroy the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]] near the battle's climax, an order never carried out before the Death Star's own destruction.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Sir, the deflector shield is down, and we've lost all contact with the generating station.''"<br />"''Position the station to blow up the moon.''"<br />"''Commence rotation of main batteries.|Lieutenant Endicott and Moff Tiaan Jerjerrod, during the Battle of Endor|<ref name="Blu-ray">{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars: The Complete Saga|scene=Jerjerrod's Conflict|nolink=1}}</ref>}}
The [[Human/Legends|Human]]  [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="ROTJ" /> Endicott was an orphan who attended the prestigious [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]],<ref name="Death Star II" /> the toughest [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] training facility in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' {{C|"Felth, Davin"}}</ref> After graduating third in his class from the Academy, Endicott was offered a [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]] position on the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], in construction over the remote [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|235|Endicott, Lieutenant}}</ref>

[[File:ScrewYouStormies-ROTJBR.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Endicott reports to Commander Jerjerrod in the Death Star control room during the Battle of Endor.]]
In early [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] to the beginning of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].</ref> Endicott, a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]],<ref name="Death Star II" /> was on duty within the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star's]] [[Death Star command center|control room]], supervising a group of [[Controller/Legends|controllers]] monitoring the battlestation's surrounding [[Realspace/Legends|space]] traffic, when he oversaw the arrival of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[ST 321/Legends|personal shuttle]] aboard one of the Death Star's hangars. Vader's visit came completely unannounced in an effort to remedy the Death Star's lagging construction schedule. Once Endicott realized that an approaching [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] bearing a class-one priority ranking and requesting for the Death Star to deactivate its [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]] was carrying the Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lord]], he ordered [[Jad Bean/Legends|Jad Bean]], a nearby shield operator, to notify [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod/Legends|Tiaan Jerjerrod]], the Death Star's [[Commander/Legends|commander]], of their distinguished guest's arrival. Endicott then proceeded to head toward the docking bay and Vader's [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]].<ref name="ROTJ novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref>

During the subsequent [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the climactic confrontation between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], Endicott was again present within the Death Star's control room, serving under Jerjerrod's direct command. He stood near Jerjerrod when [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], also present aboard, issued the order for the Death Star to first fire its [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser|superlaser]] upon the attacking [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]], revealing to the Rebels the battlestation's operational status.<ref name="ROTJ" />

As the battle raged, the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] commanded Jerjerrod to use the Death Star to blow up the Endor [[Moon/Legends|moon]] should the Rebels succeed in destroying the [[Endor shield generator bunker|shield generator]] there protecting the battlestation from direct assault, which indeed soon occurred.<ref name="ROTJ novel" /> Upon seeing that the shield was down, Endicott immediately notified Jerjerrod, adding that the Death Star had lost contact with the generating station. As instructed, Jerjerrod then ordered Endicott to position the Death Star to destroy the moon, which Endicott relayed to Bean.<ref name="Blu-ray" /> Before Jerjerrod could execute the order to obliterate Endor, however, the Rebels instead destroyed the Death Star, [[Death/Legends|killing]] the Emperor, Vader, and Jerjerrod in a sweeping victory.<ref name="ROTJ novel" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Vader!|Endicott's surprised reaction to Darth Vader's arrival|<ref name="ROTJ novel" />}}
Endicott, a docking bay [[Technician/Legends|technician]],<ref name="Death Star II" /> displayed a certain shock of recognition, exclaiming [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader's name aloud to himself, upon realizing that the Dark Lord had suddenly and unexpectedly arrived aboard the Death Star.<ref name="ROTJ novel" /> Later, while Commander Jerjerrod held visible misgivings regarding the Emperor's directive to destroy Endor, and thereby kill the many Imperial personnel stationed on the moon, Endicott, by comparison, demonstrated no hesitation in relaying Jerjerrod's command to ready the Death Star for firing.<ref name="Blu-ray" />

Unlike many Imperial [[Officer/Legends|officers]],<ref name="ROTJ" /><ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> Endicott did not speak with a [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] accent.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Endicott had [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]],<ref name="ROTJ" /><ref name="Blu-ray" /> blue [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and light skin.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Equipment==
Lieutenant Endicott wore the black variant of the standard-issue [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|Imperial officer's uniform]], sans [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank insignia]], and a chrome [[Utility belt/Legends|utility belt]] during his service aboard the Death Star.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:GlynBaker.png|thumb|right|235px|English actor Glyn Baker, pictured here at a 2013 fan convention, played Lieutenant Endicott in ''Return of the Jedi''.]]
The Endicott character appears briefly, without name, in the opening scenes of the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] as the docking bay control officer who orders that Commander Jerjerrod be informed of Darth Vader's arrival aboard the Death Star. The character appears again, fleetingly, in the background of the battlestation's control room as the Death Star first fires its superlaser during the Battle of Endor.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Actor [[Glyn Baker]] portrayed Endicott in the film<ref name="Glyn Baker interview">{{YouTube|video=wLiHCysBXkc|text=Glyn Baker Interview - 002 The Living Daylights, Star Wars Return of The Jedi & The Wild Geese|channel=@FlicksAndTheCity|name=Flicks And The City|quote=Glyn Baker interview about playing 002 on The Living Daylights, Lt Endcott on the set of Star Wars Return of the Jedi & his first film The Wild Geese. Glyn also chats about Star Wars Episodes 7, 8 & 9 and the 50th James Bond anniversary.}} [[Wookieepedia:Interview/Endicott/Glyn Baker interview transcript|transcript]].</ref> without credit.<ref name="ROTJ" /> The Endicott character first appeared, unnamed, in the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Return of the Jedi'' novelization]], written by [[James Kahn]]<ref name="ROTJ novel" /> and published just prior to the film's theatrical release.<ref name="ROTJ release date">According to [http://www.amazon.com/Star-Wars-Return-James-Kahn/dp/0345307674 Amazon.com], the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Return of the Jedi'' novelization's]] first edition release was on [[May 12]], [[1983]], while the [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'' film]] debuted on [[May 25]], 1983, according to [https://lucasfilm.com/star-wars-episode-6-return-of-the-jedi Lucasfilm.com].</ref>

Endicott was first identified by name and provided a brief backstory on the [http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/DeathStarII-Dark/large/lieutenantendicott.gif "Lieutenant Endicott" card] as part of the [[July]] [[2000]] ''[[Death Star II Limited]]'' expansion set of the ''[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]''.<ref name="Death Star II" />

===Deleted scene===
Endicott was originally slated to appear in an additional film scene in the Death Star's control room during the Battle of Endor alongside Jerjerrod, in which he informs Jerjerrod that the Endor shield generator protecting the Death Star has been destroyed, and then proceeds to relay Jerjerrod's subsequent command to prepare the battlestation to obliterate the moon. While this scene was filmed, it was ultimately cut from the final version of ''Return of the Jedi''. This deleted scene was officially released as part of the [[2011]] ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' [[Wikipedia:Blu-ray Disc|Blu-ray]] set.<ref name="Blu-ray" />

With regards to [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]], [[Lucasfilm]] continuity manager [[Leland Chee]] stated on his [[StarWars.com]] blog that the deleted scenes of the six ''[[Star Wars]]'' films that have been publicly released are "[[Canon|G-canon]]," or "[[George Lucas]] Canon," meaning that the related material originated with Lucas and is therefore considered the highest tier of canonicity, unless the deleted scenes "conflict with something else seen in the films or if the reasoning behind deleting the scene keeps it from being continuity."<ref name="Chee-SW.com">{{Blog|holocron|33|What'd I say again? Select posts by me regarding continuity}}</ref> Given Chee's declaration, this article treats the Endicott deleted scene as full canon in the absence of any contradictory elements.

In the Endicott deleted scene,<ref name="Blu-ray" /> actor Glyn Baker, who portrays the character,<ref name="Glyn Baker interview" /> clearly speaks with a [[Wikipedia:British English|British accent]],<ref name="Blu-ray" /> while in the theatrical version of the film, the character speaks with an [[Wikipedia:American English|American accent]], suggesting that Baker's voice was dubbed for the film's final release.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Due to the unfinished nature of the deleted scenes, this article considers Endicott's accent from the final version of the film to be correct.
